core_obligations: Define the functor F sending a ring to the quotient of a polynomial ring by the monic polynomials over it, and record that F(A) contains A, is free as an A-module and is a filtered colimit of finite free A-algebras (proof lines 3580-3590).
Form the colimit B of the sequence of iterates of F along the natural inclusions (proof lines 3590-3595).
Show that every monic polynomial over B has coefficients in a finite stage and hence a root in the next stage, so that B is absolutely integrally closed (proof lines 3595-3600).
Record that the remaining properties are left to the reader as the author does (proof lines 3600-3602).
proof_roadmap: Define F and its basic properties (proof lines 3580-3590).
Take the colimit of the iterates (proof lines 3590-3595).
Use stability of coefficients and roots to conclude (proof lines 3595-3602).
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs, for an arbitrary ring, an extension that is a filtered colimit of finite free algebras, is free as a module and is absolutely integrally closed, and the proof is a 23-line construction. It defines an endofunctor of the category of rings by adjoining a formal root of every monic polynomial, observes that it is free and a filtered colimit of finite free algebras, and then takes the colimit of the resulting sequence; any monic polynomial over the colimit has coefficients in some finite stage and therefore acquires a root at the next stage, which makes the colimit absolutely integrally closed. The functor and the colimit argument are displayed, and the remaining properties are declared to be left to the reader.
